_comment: Pattern rules for POCUS utilization log analysis. Each event has per-vendor patterns and optional exclude_patterns. Weights: 1.0=definitive, 0.7-0.9=strong, 0.3-0.6=supporting/contextual.

_timestamp_formats._comment: One entry per vendor. 'regex' must have exactly one capture group covering the full timestamp text (including any separators like ',' before milliseconds). 'strptime' parses that captured text directly - literal separator characters (comma, slash, period) go straight into the format string, no need to normalize them in code. Each vendor maps to a LIST of format entries (not a single entry) - files from the same vendor can use different timestamp formats (e.g. Sonosite's CSV export vs. its native system.log), and each is tried in order until one matches a given line.

Mindray_M6.note: Identical bracket format to standard Mindray - kept as a separate entry in case M6 firmware diverges in a future sample

GE.note: GE Venue Go: 'Weekday,Mon DD HH:MM:SS.mmm,YYYY' - timestamp is not at the start of the line, so no leading ^ anchor

Sonosite.note: Sonosite CSV: 'LogType,YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffff,...' - 4-digit fractional seconds, strptime's %f left-justifies into microseconds so this parses correctly without modification

Sonosite native system.log (C++ application trace log, distinct from the CSV export): 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS - message'. No fractional seconds, but session-gap/window analysis operates in minutes, so second-level resolution is sufficient.

exam_started.description: New patient/exam created on the device

patterns.note: Patient record successfully created (manual entry)
Patient selected from MWL worklist - highest documentation signal
New patient created manually from current patient tab
Patient session started — definitive exam open signal
Patient entry screen opened — user is entering/selecting patient

TENTATIVE — older M6 firmware has no doppler.metrics.* channel like standard Mindray, so no clean patient-registration signal was found. This only confirms the iStation patient-import dialog was opened, not that a patient was actually selected. Recommend revisiting if a stronger signal turns up in future M6 samples.

patterns.regex: Study created; Sono Study Instance UID
patterns.note: ePHI stream: study record created with Study Instance UID — UID is generated regardless of PHI-export setting, so this is the most reliable exam-start signal
Corroborating: user completed the patient info entry screen

Found in a second, larger batch of real logs to be the dominant patient-registration signal by far (2750 occurrences vs. 280 for NEW_REGISTERED_PATIENT in that batch). Appears to double-fire per actual add action (an ERROR-type echo plus a STATUS-type confirmation with a real patient ID, ~200ms apart) so weighted as corroborating rather than 1.0 definitive.
Corroborating: new patient registered on RSI event bus — sometimes fires with placeholder parameter value, treated as supporting signal only

exam_ended_by_user.description: User explicitly pressed the End Exam button

patterns.note: Physical or touch End Exam button pressed by user
User logout — implies end of exam session; closest Mindray proxy to end-exam
Patient entry screen closed — exam committed and dismissed
User pressed the End Exam action — direct analog to GE's PatientEndExamCtrl

exam_completed.description: Exam/study successfully committed and closed by the system

patterns.regex: EPM_CMD_EndPatient.*Study with UID .* has been closed
patterns.note: Study UID closed - definitive exam commit confirmation
Exam mode committed to metrics — fires when exam is formally recorded
Image committed to DICOM spooler — strongest available exam completion signal on LOGIQ e

patterns.regex: Exam completed; Sono Study Instance UID
patterns.note: ePHI stream: processEndExamComplete — system confirmation that the study was committed/closed, same Study UID as exam_started
Corroborating: patient registration ended on the RSI event bus — found in a second larger batch of real logs (180 occurrences)

patterns.regex: Exam completed for Study Instance UID .+, patientLoid \d+
patterns.note: From Sonosite's native system.log (APtManager.cpp) - a separate, complementary log file from the CSV export, same physical devices. Definitive: real Study UID attached. 142 occurrences in the validating sample.

exam_save_failed.description: Exam save failed - study not committed to local archive

patterns.note: Explicit save failure - exam data may be lost
Duplicate StudyInstanceUID - likely a reconnect/retry collision
From Sonosite's native system.log (TDicomManager.cpp) - archive/PACS send attempt failed. Genuine negative signal: proof a save was attempted, distinct from never attempting one at all.
From system.log (tDicomContextTransfer.cpp) - corroborating: fires alongside the STORAGE transfer failure above in the same error burst
Hardware-level scan start - most reliable scan event
Hardware-level scan start — transducer actively transmitting
Scanner hardware initialized and ready — fires once per boot/restart of imaging
Live imaging began — direct analog to GE's startScan/Mindray's StartScan

Live imaging started — also fires on unfreeze/resume-live on this firmware (M6 doesn't log freeze/unfreeze as distinct events from scan start/stop), validated against real M6 data: rapid StartScan/StopScan pairs (as fast as ~50ms apart) confirm deliberate user toggling, not idle timeout

freeze_pressed.description: User manually froze the image (live -> frozen). Also carries probe and application context.

patterns.note: State transition Live->Freeze with probe+application context embedded
User-initiated freeze — hardware freeze command issued
Replay log freeze event — includes exam/probe context fields
Live->Freeze state transition with probe and application context — same ESStatus format as Venue Go
Explicit freeze signal, found in a second larger batch of real logs (602 occurrences) — replaces the earlier tentative RSIEVENT_STOP_CAPTURE-based guess, which is demoted to corroborating-only below
Demoted from the earlier tentative primary mapping now that SYSEVENT_IMG_IMAGING_FREEZE is confirmed as the definitive signal; kept only as a weak corroborating signal

Live imaging stopped/frozen — pairs with scan_started's StartScan. Note: 'Enter/Exit Freeze Power-Save Mode' lines are a secondary power-state echo of this same action on M6, not an independent signal, so they're intentionally left unmapped to avoid double-counting
State transition Freeze->Live with probe+application context
Replay log unfreeze — user resumed live imaging
Freeze->Live state transition — user resumed live imaging

User resumed live imaging from frozen state — found alongside IMAGING_FREEZE in a second larger batch of real logs, notably lower volume (52) than FREEZE (602), meaning not every freeze is followed by a captured unfreeze in these samples

autofreeze.description: System automatically froze due to inactivity - not a user scan event

patterns.note: Inactivity autofreeze - signals idle machine, not scanning
Autofreeze control event
Inactivity autofreeze — not a user scan event

image_saved.description: User pressed the image store/save button

patterns.note: User triggered async image store - primary save signal
Image/cine save initiated — path encodes patient folder, exam type, and sequence
Image written to local ImageBuffer — user pressed store/print button
User pressed the image/clip capture button — primary save signal
User pressed the clip/cine capture button — companion action to IMAGE_CAPTURE for cine loops specifically, found in a second larger batch of real logs (40 occurrences)
Identical channel/message to standard Mindray — the save subsystem didn't change on M6, only the exam-lifecycle/scan channel did

image_archived_local.description: Image file successfully written to local device archive

patterns.note: DCM file committed to local archive - confirms local storage
Save completed — file successfully written to local storage
Image successfully saved to disk (ImageBuffer or Spooler)
Save confirmed complete — confirms local storage write finished
Clip save reported nominal status — supporting signal for cine/clip saves specifically
Identical to standard Mindray — save completed to local storage
Explicit save-success confirmation, one step after FinishSaveSysFile in the observed sequence

dicom_spooled_for_send.description: Image converted and staged in DICOM spooler for outbound send

patterns.note: Image converted to DICOM and placed in spooler queue for PACS send

worklist_queried.description: Device queried the DICOM Modality Worklist (MWL) for patient orders

patterns.note: MWL association opened - device is pulling scheduled exams
MWL returned results - count of scheduled procedures available

probe_connected.description: Probe physically connected or detected on a connector

patterns.note: Probe physically detected on connector with name and ID
Transducer usage metric: probe name, serial number, and scan frame count

application_context.description: Imaging application/preset active (e.g. Cardiac, Abdo, Vein_VA). Extracted from ESStatus lines alongside freeze events.

patterns.note: Application became active - use to tag scan sessions with exam type
Active probe and exam mode together — fires on preset/mode change

Preset/exam-type selected — only 54% co-occurrence with an active imaging interval (often selected during setup, before live imaging), so treated as workflow context rather than proof of active scanning
From Sonosite's native system.log (uScanheadModel.cpp) - preset/exam-type selection, same tier as the CSV export's SET_EXAM_TYPE_BY_NAME above

From system.log - worklist-item validation warnings (missing/incomplete DICOM fields). Validated: these bursts consistently land 5-90 seconds before a 'Selected exam' event across many different days, so they're event-tied rather than periodic background noise - but the message content itself is a warning about incomplete data, not confirmation of successful worklist use, hence the low weight.

patterns.regex: Event:GUI Dialog Showup\]\s*\{\{Probe and Exam Mode\}\}
patterns.note: User opened the probe/exam-mode selection screen — workflow context, not proof of active scanning on its own

Exam-type preset selected from the Probe and Exam Mode list. Originally matched only 'EM ...' presets (site-specific names: EM SOFT TISSUE, EM FAST etc.); widened because a real M6 with stock presets logs plain names like {{Lung}} and {{Adult Cardiac  *}}. Logged as [type:USR] on real units and [type:SYS] in the sample, so the type tag is not matched.
System applied probe + exam mode (logged at INFO at boot/probe activation, e.g. 'exam mode:PED_ABD_EXAM'). Context only.

image_adjustment.description: User adjusted an imaging acquisition parameter

patterns.note: Named parameter change with probe and application context
User opened measurement menu — indicates active clinical use
User opened report/worksheet dialog — strong documentation signal

Broadened from an initial 3-pattern set (gain/depth/cine) after a second, larger batch of real logs surfaced 47 total SET/TOGGLE/RESET parameter-change variants (color gain, Doppler PRF, zoom, sector steering, needle guide, mode toggles, etc.). The original 3 were validated at 99.9-100% co-occurrence with active imaging; this broader pattern follows the same semantic (user actively changing an image parameter) so is trusted at a slightly lower weight pending the same clustering test on the new variants. application_context's SET_EXAM_TYPE_BY_NAME pattern is listed earlier in this file and claims that specific line first, so it won't double-fire here.

User ran a Smart (AI) measurement tool - these operate on a live/just-acquired image, so they imply active scanning. Key signal on M6 units logging at INFO level, where the TRACE-level UImgController::StartScan!/StopScan! lines are absent. Only the [type:USR] PushButton line is matched; the [type:SYS] Peek UI1 and operation.replay echoes of the same press are not, to avoid double counting.
User pressed the B-mode imaging button - supporting evidence of live imaging on INFO-level M6 logs.

system_boot.description: System finished booting and is ready for use

patterns.note: System fully initialized - use as session start boundary
Application started — session boundary
System fully initialized — session boundary
System fully initialized and ready — session start boundary
Application started — session boundary. Same banner as standard Mindray; confirmed in a real M6 log (Oct 2026).

system_shutdown.description: System is shutting down. Mode indicates reason (e.g. shutdownlowbattery).

patterns.note: System shutdown with reason code - shutdownlowbattery is common POCUS pattern
Graceful shutdown initiated — session boundary
Graceful shutdown or battery shutdown initiated
Battery-triggered shutdown — device ran out of power
Graceful shutdown initiated — session boundary

Voice-assist feature state chatter
Raw touch coordinates — high volume, no clinical value
Patient list UI refresh chatter, not a clinical event itself
UI navigation chatter
Power-state polling, not user-driven
DICOM backend component-ready — subsumed by system_boot's SYSTEM_READY
Raw touch/gesture replay telemetry — 99.8% of this vendor's log volume in samples seen so far, no clinical value
Touch activity chatter outside the replay channel too

patterns.regex: PSC:Enter Idle|PSC:Exit Idle|PSC:Enter ScreenSaver|PSC:Exit ScreenSaver|screen saver state
patterns.note: Power/screensaver state chatter
Power-state echoes — the freeze/unfreeze action itself is captured by StartScan/StopScan, this is a secondary state indicator only
Recurring hardware-module-absent error, not user-driven (note: vendor's own typo 'modual' preserved literally)

patterns.regex: The funcid\(\d+\) setting state is not exist
patterns.note: Internal UI state-machine noise, different wording than standard Mindray's uef.base Thread noise but same category of chatter
Probe inventory self-check — validated as firing on wake/boot (34 occurrences, consistently aligned with activity-burst starts), not a discrete per-scan probe-selection action

user_login.description: User logged into the device — session boundary and authentication event

patterns.note: User login recorded in metrics — identifies operator and marks session start
